title: Brown rice flour, coarse ground, pre-gelatinized, organic

content.title: About
content.content: Coarse ground brown rice flour is an organic product made from whole brown rice that has been pre‑gelatinized to improve water absorption and texture. It has a mild nutty aroma, light brown color, and is suitable for gluten‑free recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice flour retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice flour.
Pre‑gelatinization helps it dissolve easily in liquids and improves baked goods structure.
Organic certification guarantees no synthetic pesticides or GMOs.
Rice flour is widely used in Asian cuisine for noodles, pancakes, and desserts.
Coarse grinding preserves a more pronounced flavor and texture compared with fine flour.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Provides a good amount of fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Delivers slow‑releasing energy, helpful for blood sugar management.

items.title: Contains magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for bone and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Suitable for low‑fat diets while still offering nutritional value.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Safe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to rice flour.

items.title: Slightly higher glycemic index after gelatinization
items.content: Pre‑gelatinization can modestly increase the product’s glycemic impact.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: As with most rice products, trace amounts of arsenic may be present; a varied diet is recommended.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the flour in gluten‑free breads, pancakes, muffins, coatings, and sauces. The pre‑gelatinized nature helps bind ingredients and gives baked goods a tender crumb. It blends well with other gluten‑free flours such as corn or tapioca.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
